rules: Pick cards
Add up every keyword that points at the same card page. Keep the top 120 pages by total searches.
One page per card. The most searched cards first.
Match the card
Search PriceCharting for the card name (+ set if the URL has one). English cards only. No boxes, tins, packs or World Championships deck reprints. Card name must match exactly.
The same name exists in many sets and languages. Picking the wrong one shows the wrong price.
Match the card
If the URL names a set, take the most valuable printing in that set.
That is the chase card people search for.
Match the card
If the URL has no set, compare the 3 most valuable printings and keep the one with the most money traded per week (price x sales).
Keeps the card people actually buy, not a cheap bulk copy or a one-off rarity.
Match the card
Collector nicknames (Bubble Mew, Van Gogh Pikachu) use a lookup table. Unclear nicknames are settled by what Google shows in its top results.
Price sites do not know nicknames. Google does.
Google data
Use the Google results saved during keyword research. Only search again if a keyword has no saved result.
No repeated spend.
CardOutpost data

Pull odds, pulls, vault copies and pack are MOCK until CardOutpost connects its database. The Premium pack price ($25) and max pull ($250) are real. Sell-back (100%) and lowest listing (50%) follow the real FAQ rules.
We have no access to CardOutpost data. Columns keep the same names when the real data arrives.
CardOutpost data
A card goes in the cheapest pack whose max pull covers its value.
A $1,288 card cannot sit in a pack whose max pull is $250.
One page per card

If two of our URLs land on the same printing, the URL that names the set is the main page (if both or neither do, the one with more searches). The other gets a canonical tag pointing to it and stays out of the sitemap.
Two pages about the same card compete with each other. Google picks one anyway. We decide which.
Title
"[Card] [Set] #[No.] Price: PSA 10 $[price] | CardOutpost". If over 60 characters, drop the price, then the set.
Google cuts titles near 60 characters. The price in the title answers the search before the click.
H1
"[Card] #[No.] ([Set])".
Names the exact printing. Clear for the reader and for Google.
Meta description
Raw price, PSA 10 price, number of 10s, and CardOutpost pull odds. Under 155 characters.
Shows numbers no other result shows: the odds.
URL
Keep the URL from the keyword research: /cards/[set]/[card] or /cards/[card].
Already planned and mapped to keywords in Part 2.
Page order

1 H1 and image. 2 Price box (PSA 10, raw, 12-month trend, date). 3 One selling line and the pack button. 4 "About this card" bullets. 5 Grade ladder. 6 Price history chart. 7 CardOutpost data. 8 FAQ. 9 Related cards and links up. 10 Source and disclaimer note.
Price sites and retailers all keep the top for the price and the buy button. Text goes right under it, as bullets, never at the bottom only. No competitor has 3, 7 or 8.
Selling line
One line, never a paragraph: pack, pack price, odds, "shown before you open", vaulted and insured, sell back at 100%.
Fits the first phone screen next to the button. Odds next to the claim keeps it honest and matches the responsible-play page.
About this card
6 to 8 bullets, each one fact from the data: set and release, rarity, price now and 12-month trend, grade 10 count and share, sales speed, CardOutpost odds and pulls. 120 to 180 words.
Amazon, Target and Walmart put the first text right under the buy box as bullets. Each bullet is a different number per card, so no two pages read the same.
Grade ladder
Table of prices for ungraded, grade 7, 8, 9, 9.5 and PSA 10, each with the PSA population for that grade. Stacked rows on phones.
The main thing people look for on a card price search. PriceCharting, the biggest ranker, leads with it.
Worth grading?
Expected value after grading = (gem rate x PSA 10 price) + ((1 - gem rate) x grade 9 price) - $25 fee. Compare with the raw price.
A clear yes/no with the maths shown.
FAQ: fixed
Every page has 3 fixed questions: worth (raw and PSA 10), how many 10s exist, pull odds on CardOutpost. One number per answer, with the date.
One card, one fact, one number per answer is the shape AI Overviews and LLMs extract best. FAQPage schema labels it for them.
FAQ: from Google

Up to 2 more from Google's "People also ask", after 4 steps. Filter: the question must be about this exact card and answerable from our data. Merge: questions that mean the same thing become one. Rewrite: standard wording with the exact card name. Answer: only from our numbers; if there is no data, the question is dropped.
Google's questions are real but sometimes junk (other cards, sealed boxes). The layers keep only what we can answer honestly.
FAQ: display
FAQ text is visible in the page code (tap to open on phones) and worded differently from the bullets.
Google ignores hidden FAQ text, and repeated text looks thin.
Schema
Product (with AggregateOffer from lowest listing to market value), FAQPage, BreadcrumbList. JSON-LD.
Required by the brief. Lets Google show price and breadcrumbs.
Links
Breadcrumb: Home > Cards > [Set] > [Card]. Link up to the set page and the Pokemon page if they exist in our page plan.
Set and Pokemon pages are how Google finds card pages.
Links
Related cards: up to 4 other cards of the same Pokemon, then up to 4 from the same set, most searched first. Only pages that pass the quality gate.
Spreads authority to the cards people search most. Never links to a noindex page.
Links
Call to action: "Rip the [pack] pack" to /select, shown with the odds. Also a sticky bottom bar on phones.
Turns a price search into a pack opening. The button is always one tap away.
Quality gate
Index only if ALL pass: a real market price, CardOutpost odds present, not a duplicate, "About this card" text under 80% the same as any other page.
Thin or duplicate pages never ship. A rare card that sells once a month is not thin, so sales speed and grade counts are not gate rules: those sections are simply hidden when the data is missing.
Quality gate
A page that fails gets noindex, stays out of the sitemap, and gets no internal links. It is rechecked every refresh.
It can pass later when data arrives.
Sitemap
Only indexable pages, with lastmod = the date the prices were fetched.
Tells Google which pages matter and when they changed.
Mobile

First phone screen holds only: H1 (2 lines max), small image, price box with 2 numbers, the selling line, the button. Sticky bottom bar with pack, price and odds. Grade ladder as stacked rows. Chart loads when scrolled to. FAQ tap-to-open with text in the page code. 16px text, 44px tap targets, fixed image box so nothing jumps.
Most card searches happen on phones. A phone screen is about 640px after the header, so nothing else fits above the fold.
Mobile
All content is in the HTML, not built by JavaScript. Test every template change with Lighthouse mobile and on a real phone.
Fixes audit issue 5 and keeps pages fast on 4G.
